resources.string: Lens flares: faint coloured rings across the picture from the brightest lights, as a camera lens makes them. Halos + lens flares: also a soft glow with a fine star at candles, torches and lamps.
H:M:S is the game\'s own play time: every save keeps it (typewriter and instant save), as on the GameCube. Time in this menu or with the app in the background does not count.

Performance cores: the game and the graphics run on the phone\'s fastest cores and ask Android for higher clocks. Smoother on many phones, but it needs more CPU power and the device gets warmer. Default: Android decides.

Weather effects: fog banks, rain, water spray. Special effects: steam, heat shimmer, water. Particle effects: blood, dust, smoke, splashes, sparks and fire; Less draws half of them, None leaves out all but fire and explosions, which stay at half as a warning. Shadows & light: off leaves out shadows (also in cut scenes), lens glows and light shafts; the rooms keep their lighting. Each saves graphics work on weaker devices; the spot where a shot hits, hints, the laser and every effect in cut scenes stay.

View distance: Medium and Short bring the distance fog nearer, and what lies beyond it is not drawn. That helps where the processor or the number of objects holds the game back, on slower phones at a low resolution: in the village about half of the objects go. At a high resolution the graphics chip is busy with the pixels and gains little. Rooms without distance fog, and those whose fog lies far beyond what you see (the castle, the island), stay as they are.
Resolution: %1$d × %2$d pixels (level %3$s) · screen %4$d × %5$d · applies when the menu closes. Higher levels need more power.
Resolution: %1$d × %2$d pixels (level %3$s, Dynamic) · screen %4$d × %5$d · applies when the menu closes. Dynamic goes a level lower while the GPU cannot keep up.
RE: a symbol for what each button does (the default); GC: the letters in the GameCube\'s colours, as before. The editor (the gear at the top right) has the same switch.
Auto: shown without a controller, a tap shows them, a button hides them. Force: always shown. Suppress: hidden while a controller is connected. MENU = SELECT.
Auto aim: when you raise your weapon, the aim jumps to the nearest enemy in front of you and follows it for a moment (the game\'s own lock-on).
Always run: Leon runs whenever you move; hold the run button (e.g. B) to walk instead.
Keeps the shoulder camera a little further behind Leon while walking and standing. Aiming and tight spots bring it close as before; it moves smoothly in between.

Touch Aiming: while L or R holds a weapon ready, the touch area aims by swipes on the right half (the aim follows your finger and stops when it stops) or the touch C stick aims like a stick (add it with the gear at the top right). Move Stick: as on the GameCube.
Alternate Controls: L1 = Knife, L2 = Aim (aim with the right stick), R1 = Inventory (Weapons/Recovery), R2 = Fire / use the knife, Y = Map. A, B, X (Ashley) and START as before.
Knife by Swipe: a quick swipe across the picture draws the knife and slashes; swipe upward or downward to slash high or low.
Latch: one press (button or touch) holds L, R or B until the next press (B latched: Leon keeps running).

Invert vertical and Aim speed: for aiming the knife and the weapons by touch or with a controller, not with the gyro. Invert vertical applies to the mouse too (aiming and binoculars); its speed is the Mouse Sensitivity. Invert vertical sets the game\'s own option.
The newest release opens on GitHub: download the APK there and install it.
Export and Import Player Data: your saves as .gci (for Dolphin or GameCube) and a touch layout of your own as CubeEvil4-touch-layout.json. The import brings both back.
The card is in use (the game saves or loads) or the game is still loading – close the menu and open it again in a moment.
To play another version: the game ends, and you import both of its discs on the start screen. Saves, memory card and settings stay.
The game ends and the start screen opens: import both discs there, then start the game. Progress not saved is lost; saves, memory card and settings stay.

Music is the background music; sound effects are everything else in the game (shots, voices, steps). The movies keep their sound as it is. The two buttons switch the music or the sound effects off entirely; switched on again, they play at the volume above.
Extra in-between pictures. The game logic stays at 30 frames/s.
This screen runs at %1$d Hz: 60 FPS cannot be shown evenly on it and may stutter. 30 FPS (60 FPS off) runs smoother here.

Smooths jagged edges in a last step. Works with or without MSAA; the picture gets slightly softer.
Filters change the look of the whole picture and can be combined.
Sharpen brings back the detail of textures that gets soft when the picture is enlarged to the screen (mostly in the wide picture formats). Movies stay as they are.
CRT: the picture as an old tube TV showed it, with lines, a curved screen and a soft glow. The touch controls and the minimap stay sharp.
Warm film brings out the browns and golds; Survival horror pales the colours and hardens the contrast. Strength sets how much.
Frame skip Normal: while the graphics chip lags, a finished picture is left out so the game keeps its normal speed.
Frame skip Aggressive: the game itself leaves out at most every second picture while it falls behind; this also saves processor time and is much faster on phones with a slow processor.
Vulkan only: after the picture is cleared, the graphics chip no longer loads it again, which saves memory bandwidth on Mali and Adreno chips. The picture stays the same.
Frame skip and 60 FPS exclude each other: switching one on switches the other off.
Merges several objects into one call to the graphics driver. Can help phones with a slow graphics driver (e.g. Mali GPUs) and may cost a little on others. No effect while 60 FPS is on.

Sends each picture\'s vertex data to the graphics chip through one buffer that stays mapped, instead of a new buffer every picture. Can save time on Mali GPUs and uses a little more graphics memory. Takes effect at once.

With Vulkan, Merge draw calls and Vertex ring buffer are greyed out and not used: Vulkan always sends the vertex data through a buffer that stays mapped, and its draw calls are cheap, so merging would only add pipelines to build. Your choice comes back with OpenGL ES.
The language of the game\'s texts and subtitles. Device language: the device\'s language if the game has it, English otherwise. A change restarts the game.
The new language is used after a restart of the game. Progress since your last save is lost.

The game stopped at %1$s (Disc %2$d): in the disc image you imported, this file differs from the original disc, so the image is damaged. Dump your Disc %2$d again (or take another intact copy) and import it again on the start screen. Your saves stay.
The game stopped at %1$s (Disc %2$d): the copy of this file on this device is damaged (it changed after the import). Import Disc %2$d again on the start screen. Your saves stay.
The game stopped at %1$s (Disc %2$d): the file is intact, but reading it failed. Please send the error report, then start the game again.
The game stopped at %1$s (Disc %2$d): the file on this device is damaged or missing. Import Disc %2$d again on the start screen. Your saves stay.

The switches stay on until you switch them off; your save does not keep them. Some attacks still kill Leon at once (a chainsaw, a grab, a boulder). The buttons change your game: the weapon, the case and the money stay in your next save. Automatic QTEs presses the buttons of every quick-time prompt for you. Unlock extra games adds Assignment Ada and The Mercenaries to the title menu, as after finishing the game; your next save keeps them. Invisibility: enemies take no notice of you and do not attack; bosses and scripted scenes still can.
%1$s already owned: now at its highest levels.
Not now: only while Leon plays, not in the case, the map or a movie.
No room in the attaché case.
Will be done as soon as the game runs.
This game core has no cheats.

Random items: the items lying in the story\'s rooms (ammo, herbs and other recovery items, grenades, pesetas, treasures) are dealt anew in every room you enter from then on, and a room always gives the same items until you switch this off and on again. Keys, weapons, files and other story items stay as they are, so the game can always be finished. Items you already picked up stay picked up; enemies, barrels and boxes keep their own drops. Not in Assignment Ada and The Mercenaries.
Assignment Ada and The Mercenaries are unlocked (Professional as well, as after finishing the game). The title menu shows them after a restart. Progress since your last save is lost.
Unlocked: Assignment Ada and The Mercenaries are in the title menu after the next restart.
Already unlocked: Assignment Ada and The Mercenaries are in the title menu.

The character takes Leon\'s place in the story at once: the room loads again where you stand (during a cutscene, from the next room on). Leon\'s case, life and money stay; weapons the character has no model of its own for show Leon\'s. Krauser brings his bow: each room start gives it back and fills his arrows up to 40; with anyone else it leaves the case, and saves never keep it. Wesker brings his silencer the same way and puts it on the handgun; it too leaves the case with anyone else and is never saved. Both come only where the case has room; otherwise at the next room start. Ashley\'s part stays Ashley\'s, cutscenes and radio calls still show Leon. Your saves always keep Leon, so they load as whoever is chosen here. Characters other than Leon are not made for the main game, so choosing one shows a warning first: \"I understand\" switches, Back keeps your current character. Special costumes: Leon and Ashley (and Ada as a stand-in) wear their special outfits, also at once.
Warning: This character is not meant for the main game. Bugs can and will occur, and they cannot be avoided!
Button Mapping: put every action of the game on keys of your controller or keyboard.

Stick dead zone: small movements of a controller stick around its centre are ignored (for a stick that drifts or trembles). Stick range: a stick pushed this far already counts as pushed all the way, so Leon walks, runs and turns reliably even if your stick does not reach its edge. The defaults leave the sticks as they are. The touch controls are not affected.

Where you feel the game\'s vibration. Auto: in a connected controller that has its own motors (Android 12 and later), otherwise in this phone or handheld. Device: always in this phone or handheld. Controller: only in the controller (nothing if it has no motors; before Android 12 in this device). Off: no vibration. The game\'s own option Vibration can still switch it off.

Choose an action, then press its key. An action of two keys (fire, reload, slash) asks for the key to hold first, then the second. A key another action had goes to that one\'s old key. The game\'s menus keep the default; its prompts still show the GameCube buttons.
Alternate Controls are on: they keep their own layout; this one applies once they are off.
This key is fixed (D-pad, confirm, back).
Press a key of the keyboard.
Press a key of the controller.
Fixed: the arrows are the D-pad, Enter confirms, Backspace goes back.
Fixed: the left stick moves, the right stick looks, the D-pad stays the D-pad.

The mouse (Android 8 and later) belongs to the game while it runs: moving it turns the camera, while aiming it moves the aim and in the binoculars the view. Its wheel zooms the scope and the binoculars (up zooms in). The app menu (F1) frees the pointer.

Field of view: widens (+) or narrows (−) the shoulder camera\'s view by up to 15 degrees, while walking and while aiming; 0° is the game\'s own. Cutscenes, the scope and the binoculars stay as they are.

A profile sets the resolution, 60 FPS, frame skip, anti-aliasing, FXAA, texture filter, performance cores and Potato mode for this device. Changing one of these by hand makes it Custom; Custom stays saved while you try a profile.

The app measures what this device can do and suggests the best settings. The game goes to the lake\'s dock for it (rain, water, fog) and the view turns around the player. It takes about 2–3 minutes; the sound is off. Afterwards you are back where you were. B / Back cancels.

Vulkan can be faster on some devices, above all with Mali graphics. Should it not start, the game goes back to OpenGL ES by itself. A change restarts the game.
The new renderer is used after a restart of the game. Progress since your last save is lost.
Vulkan needs Android 10 and graphics with Vulkan 1.1; this device draws with OpenGL ES.
Vulkan could not start on this device. The game draws with OpenGL ES.
The game ended while it started with Vulkan. It now starts with OpenGL ES; Vulkan can be chosen again in the menu (Display).

The game keeps the shaders it built, so a scene does not stutter a second time. Clear them only if graphics errors appear after an update: the game then builds them anew, and the first scenes can stutter.
The game restarts and deletes the built shaders. It builds them anew as you play, so the first scenes can stutter. Progress since your last save is lost.
